summary_en: This phase II study tests pembrolizumab given with photon beam radiation therapy in people with muscle invasive bladder cancer whose tumor responded to chemotherapy before surgery. The goal is to help patients avoid surgical removal of the bladder. Pembrolizumab is given by IV over 30 minutes on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for up to 18 cycles, and radiation is given Monday through Friday for up to 20 treatments. The record states the total study duration is 12 months, including neoadjuvant therapy, and it does not state a primary outcome measure.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa pembrolizumab administrado junto con radioterapia de haz de fotones en personas con cáncer de vejiga que invade el músculo, cuyo tumor respondió a la quimioterapia previa a la cirugía. El objetivo es ayudar a los pacientes a evitar la extirpación quirúrgica de la vejiga. El pembrolizumab se administra por vía intravenosa durante 30 minutos el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, hasta 18 ciclos, y la radiación se aplica de lunes a viernes hasta 20 tratamientos. El registro indica que la duración total del estudio es de 12 meses, incluida la terapia neoadyuvante, y no indica una medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Muscle invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder, staged cT2 to T4a, node negative, with no distant spread
Diagnosed within 180 days before starting neoadjuvant therapy
Received 3 to 6 cycles of an FDA approved neoadjuvant chemotherapy regimen for muscle invasive bladder cancer
Clinically T0 to T1 disease after neoadjuvant therapy, confirmed by TURBT and biopsies
Age 18 or older with Zubrod performance status 0 to 2
not_for: Small cell, neuroendocrine, or plasmacytoid variant on any pathology
Prior PD-1, PD-L1, PD-L2, or CTLA-4 antibody therapy, other than neoadjuvant treatment for this bladder cancer
Other cancer or malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy, per treating physician, or steroid doses above 10 mg prednisone daily
